1	# Prelude architecture
2	
3	Prelude is a tool for designing and then building an app with an agent: you pick a project, chat with the Claude Code CLI, and watch the design appear beside the chat. It runs as one Node server (plain `node:http`, views in Eta, Koda in the page) on localhost:4200, optionally inside a Tauri desktop window. Everything it produces is files in the project's `prelude/` folder, each design worked on in its own git branch and worktree. Agent-written views render in a sandboxed child process, and each design is served on its own preview origin.
4	
5	## Layers
6	
7	1. Windows
8	2. Entry points
9	3. Pages
10	4. Agent and live state
11	5. Designs and hosting
12	6. Project files
13	7. Shared helpers
14	8. Outside
15	
16	## Principles
17	
18	- **The folder is the database.** Everything Prelude makes is a file under the project's `prelude/`, committed with the code; `~/.prelude/` holds only machine-local conveniences, so nothing is lost if it's deleted.
19	- **The server is the single source of truth for live state.** Every window (chat, pop-out, browser tab) renders from the server and re-renders on its SSE events, so no window holds state another needs.
20	- **Agent-written code never runs in the server's process.** A design's views render in a sandboxed renderer, and a host that runs them unsandboxed starts only once the person approves it.
21	- **The agent works with ordinary file tools, fenced to what it may touch.** It reads the project and the folders added as references, writes only where its mode allows, and deletes by writing a file empty.
22	- **A design's memory is its files, not a conversation.** Each session starts from NOTES.md, the views and states, so sessions on different machines and branches pick up where the work stands.
23	- **Committed files must merge cleanly.** Session folders and decision ids are random, transcripts are append-only, and there's no shared index that every session rewrites.

6	## Context
7	Sessions should show flows and maps of the parts a change touches, drawn with Prelude's own design system. The agent's words go through Koda's `renderMarkdown`, which escapes raw HTML, so the agent can't write markup into the chat and shouldn't. `renderMarkdown` turns every fence into `<pre><code class="language-x">` with its body escaped, and offers no hook. Its fence tag must be `[A-Za-z0-9_-]*` with nothing after it: anything else isn't a fence, and its closing line then opens a code block that swallows the rest of the message. I've built the Design page change, but I couldn't run anything. Whether it builds, whether the states fit the model, and how the screens compare all come from Prelude's check after this turn.

**Views** (`server/views/`)
- Ported the design's `_entry.eta` and `_live-entry.eta` over the app's.
- Added the five new partials, element for element: `_message`, `_visual-flow`, `_visual-map`, `_visual-drawing` and `_visual-unread`.
- Every other partial matched the design line for line, so I left them alone. The design's styles needed nothing new, because the flow and map come from the design system.
- `push-delta.eta` now re-renders the whole message (words and pictures) into the live entry, rather than just the words.

**Server**
- **`server/visuals.js` (new):** the architecture already listed this file but it didn't exist yet. It splits an agent's message wherever it writes a fenced block, the same way Koda's markdown does. It reads `prelude-flow-1` and `prelude-map-1` blocks, checks the parts they name, and builds what each picture needs. Anything it can't draw comes back with a "Not drawn: …" reason. It also holds the description of these formats that goes to the agent.
- **`views.js`:** `messagePieces` turns a message into its words and pictures, in the order written. It also turns the new "parts" entry into a map marked "Changed", with each part's files as its note.
- **`architecture.js`:**
  - `visualsArchitecture` gives the pictures the session branch's parts, read as they stand each time the conversation is shown. So a part renamed later turns an old picture back into the text the agent wrote.
  - `partsChanged` works out which parts a turn's changed code files belong to.
  - Flow files are now read with the same step parser as the chat's flow blocks.
- **`turns.js`:** streams the pieces, so an unfinished block shows a placeholder. After a build or fix turn it records the parts that changed (R-c1y).
- **`main.js`:** connects all of the above. A conversation about the project now gets a read-only architecture brief with the formats.
- **`agent.js`:** the design, build and fix prompts now describe the two formats to the agent. Nothing ever tells it when a picture couldn't be drawn (R-b8s).
- **`workspace.js`:** the model now has types for entries, pieces, flows and maps, plus `changes` and `streaming.pieces`.

**routes.json, RULES.md and NOTES.md**
- The page route now points at `@app/server/views/_session` and no longer has `"from"`.
- The send-message answer's transcript now uses the app's `_transcript`.
